subject: Hosted API latency SLO — short-term measurement carveout request
messages:
From: Noah Chen <noah.chen@brightbridge.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API latency SLO — short-term measurement carveout request

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — BrightBridge is excited about Redwood's hosting option. We're in the final stages of procurement but ran into a measurement issue that could block the signing of the contract this quarter unless we get a narrow exception.

Context (short): during our ingestion/onboarding spike (7–10 days) we'll run a synthetic traffic pattern that heavily biases long-context customer requests. Our observed p95 for a handful of large-batch QA runs is above the p95 target in the proposed contract, but these are expected to normalize once the steady-state traffic kicks in. The critical ask: a temporary measurement carveout for the onboarding window (proposed 72 hours) that excludes synthetic traffic from p95 aggregation so it doesn't trigger credit or termination clauses.

What we'd like from Redwood: 1) an initial yes/no on whether a 72-hour carveout is acceptable operationally, 2) any evidence you need from our team (metrics / request sampling), and 3) how you prefer this documented (amendment vs addendum).

I've attached a small metrics extract from our onboarding run and a short summary of the synthetic workload.

Attachments: brightbridge-onboarding-metrics.csv (CSV), onboarding-workload-summary.txt (text inline)

Thanks,
Noah
Noah Chen
Head of Infrastructure
BrightBridge Health
noah.chen@brightbridge.io

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
To: Noah Chen <noah.chen@brightbridge.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 12:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency SLO — short-term measurement carveout request

Hi Noah —

Appreciate the level-set and the attachments. Quick answer: we can provisionally support a short-term carveout for onboarding traffic, but we need concrete sampling and an evidence package to make this formal. To move quickly I need the following from BrightBridge:

- A 1–2 page description of the synthetic workload and how it differs from steady state (exact timestamps + client IDs)
- A filtered sample of raw request headers/seq lengths for the peak windows (we only need anonymized IDs)
- A proposed carveout window (you suggested 72 hours; confirm start/end timezone)

I'll loop in Lauren (contracts lead) and Karthik (SRE partner) to validate operational and contractual implications. I'll also attach our SLO exemption template — fill the top section and return it and we can aim for an internal sign-off within 48 hours.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You send the evidence package + filled template.
2) Karthik and I run a quick ingestion test against a staging route to validate your sample.
3) Lauren will draft a 1-page amendment to the MSA documenting the carveout window and explicit exclusion rules.

I've attached the SLO exemption template as a PDF. If everything looks good we'll produce the draft amendment and share the DocuSign link.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: slo-exemption-template.pdf (form)

From: Noah Chen <noah.chen@brightbridge.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
Cc: BrightBridge SRE Team <sre@brightbridge.io>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency SLO — short-term measurement carveout request

Hi Neha / team —

Thanks — attached is the evidence bundle you requested: a small CSV extract of requests (brightbridge-onboarding-metrics.csv) and a zipped package with aggregated logs and our internal annotation (slo-exemption-evidence.zip). The carveout window we'd like to propose is 2027-01-15T00:00:00Z through 2027-01-18T00:00:00Z (72 hours).

Notes:
- The synthetic workload is a backfilled batch that replays large multi-turn sessions (avg context length ~8k tokens) for QA; these requests are not representative of normal customer traffic.
- We have anonymized IDs in the CSV; if you need more details we can provide transient keys for the staging run only.
- We're flexible on the exact start time; the window above aligns with our deployment schedule.

Please let us know if Karthik needs anything else for the staging validation. We're under a tight procurement cadence and would like to close the deal this week if possible.

Thanks,
Noah

Attachments: brightbridge-onboarding-metrics.csv (CSV), slo-exemption-evidence.zip (zip)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>
To: Noah Chen <noah.chen@brightbridge.io>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency SLO — short-term measurement carveout request

Noah / Neha —

Thanks for the evidence. I reviewed the CSV and the SRE notes Karthik shared from the staging run. We're willing to approve a limited, documented carveout with the following conditions:

1) Timebox: 72-hour window as requested (UTC range 2027-01-15T00:00:00Z to 2027-01-18T00:00:00Z).
2) Scope: exclusion applies only to p95 measurement for contract credit calculations and will be strictly limited to requests originating from the listed client IDs in the evidence package.
3) Control: BrightBridge agrees to run the workload on a designated staging route and provide Redwood with access logs for verification.
4) Audit trail: both parties sign a one-page amendment to the MSA that enumerates the exclusion and effective timestamps. If any party detects misuse, the carveout is voided immediately.

Action items:
- Neha: I'll draft the 1-page amendment and attach the clause to the HubSpot deal.
- Noah: Please confirm the UTC start/end one final time and sign/upload the filled SLO exemption template.
- Karthik: coordinate the staging validation during the window and confirm sampling methodology.

If Noah confirms today we'll route the amendment via DocuSign and attach to deal BB-2027-034.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Contracts & GTM Ops | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.inference
Attachment: draft-slo-amendment.pdf (draft)
